test.name: A pre-1850 parentage plan does not treat an early census as naming the son
test.description: Issue #4163. A US federal census from 1790 to 1840 names only the head of household, so it can place Paul Raymond Sr. in a town but cannot name Paul Jr. as his son. q_001 asks whether the Paul Raymond who died in 1828 in Berkshire County, Massachusetts, was the father of the Paul Raymond of Bristol, Vermont, born about 1770. The localities list the 1790-1840 censuses beside probate, land and town records, and no quirk says that an early census names only the head. Synthetic scenario, no PII.

input.delegation:
Create the first research plan for q_001 — was Paul Raymond (d. 1828, Berkshire County, Massachusetts) the father of Paul Raymond of Bristol, Vermont?

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Background: a United States federal census from 1790 through 1840 names only the head of household and counts everyone else in age brackets. It can place a man in a town in a year, but it never names a child and never states a relationship. The 1850 to 1870 censuses name every household member without stating relationships; from 1880 the census states each member's relationship to the head.

FAIL Correctness if any plan item, or the plan's rationale, presents a 1790 to 1840 census as naming Paul Raymond as the son of Paul Raymond Sr., or as showing the son in his father's household as evidence of parentage.

A 1790 to 1840 census used only to place either man in a town in a given year, or described as merely consistent with the relationship, is acceptable in any position in the plan. Placing Paul Sr. in a town is a legitimate way to narrow the probate and land search.

The plan must include at least one record type that can name a child of Paul Raymond Sr.: his probate or estate file, a land record or deed, or town or church records. If it has none, reduce Completeness. If a census presented as parentage evidence comes before every such record, FAIL Correctness.
Do not reduce any score for an 1850 or later census that is used correctly for what it shows.

Whether any new item was written with a status other than planned is checked by the deterministic validator test_new_plan_items_planned_status. If it fails, it is listed among the failed validators; if it is not listed, the plan met it.
The repository is irrelevant, and an item may reach a record without naming a collection id.
